description: We are a team of 4 students from RTU MIREA inspired to improve our world with AI technology. Unfortunately, we dont accept new members.
summary: Fire Atlas turns NASA microgravity combustion data into an interactive research workspace for students, researchers and aerospace engineers. It brings together BASS-II, FLEX and SAME-R: 508 test runs, 634 evidence records and 17 registered sources. Users search by fire-safety task and experimental conditions, inspect original evidence, compare investigations, explore droplet measurements and save evidence-linked answers. Mission scenarios show where results apply and where data are missing, including the lack of direct partial-gravity measurements for the Moon and Mars. A server-generated PDF preserves the sources and context of each saved answer. The English interface connects a working API, persistent workspaces and a reproducible NASA data release. The default demonstration assembles answers from reviewed findings without a generative model; optional model providers run on the server.
details:
WHAT WE BUILT

Fire Atlas is a working English-language dashboard that helps users understand microgravity combustion research through traceable evidence. The workspace connects a question to investigations, individual test runs, original sources, comparisons, mission applicability and a downloadable PDF.

NASA DATA

Our reproducible release psi-20261115-r2 contains 3 investigations, 13 materials, 508 test runs, 634 evidence records, 12 reviewed findings and 17 registered sources. BASS-II supports exploration of solid materials and flame spread, FLEX covers liquid droplets and extinction, and SAME-R covers smoke and aerosol measurements. Source identifiers, exact evidence locations and original numerical representations remain available.

HOW IT WORKS

Users search and rank relevant investigations with lexical retrieval and explicit filters for experimental conditions. They can inspect evidence, compare two or three studies and select FLEX points to open the corresponding test run. The default chart uses five control records, with the wider corpus available separately. Missing values, zeroes and unusable units remain distinct. Answers separate observations, summaries and limitations, with validated citations and numerical checks. Mission presets preserve the context of older answers. PDF reports include the workspace snapshot and registered sources.

SI USE AND SCIENTIFIC LIMITS

OpenAI Codex assisted software implementation, tests, integration, English interface copy and submission materials. SI assistance also supported data-processing code and documentation. Original NASA source files and experimental measurements were not replaced by generated measurements. The application supports server-side model providers, while the tested default offline mode assembles answers from reviewed corpus findings and clearly discloses the absence of a generative model. Online model generation requires a provider key and was not verified on this local stand. No SI-generated NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers are included.

Changing a mission scenario does not create new measurements. The interface explicitly identifies the absence of direct partial-gravity data in PSI for lunar and Martian scenarios. The product supports research discussion; it does not certify materials, predict fire probability or issue crew safety instructions.

IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION

React, TypeScript, Vite, React Router, TanStack Query, CSS Modules and Recharts power the frontend. A Python Starlette API provides persistent SQLite workspaces, background jobs, idempotency and server-generated PDF reports. OpenAPI 3.1 defines the API contract. Docker Compose starts the full service using pnpm start. A separate MSW demonstration is clearly marked.

Validation includes 37 frontend tests, 135 backend tests, 123 reasoning tests, 55 contract examples, 22 demo browser scenarios and 8 production browser scenarios. Responsive and accessibility checks cover widths from 360 to 1920 pixels. The end-to-end route reaches an original source, a FLEX measurement, comparison, an answer, a lunar scenario and a real PDF.

IMPACT

Fire Atlas reduces the effort needed to find relevant combustion studies and explain their experimental limits. It helps researchers identify useful evidence and missing conditions before selecting studies for further modeling or fire-safety research.
